claims.text: The material system is a NiFeCoCr-based high-entropy alloy containing Pd.
There is a standard baseline Pd concentration for the proposed comparison.
Increasing Pd concentration above the baseline will increase the coercive field.
Pd additions can tune magnetic behavior in the NiFeCoCrPdx alloy family.
Increasing Pd creates stronger local variations in magnetic anisotropy.
Increasing Pd creates nanoscale heterogeneities or precipitates.
The Pd-induced nanoscale heterogeneities or precipitates act as domain-wall pinning centers.
A higher Pd concentration changes the local electronic structure.
Pd addition alters the distribution of exchange energies in NiFeCoCrPdx.
Pd addition and heat treatment reduce the distribution of exchange energies and make NiFeCoCrPdx more magnetically homogeneous.
Increasing Pd increases local magnetic anisotropy.
More pronounced domain-wall pinning requires a larger external field for reversal and therefore increases coercivity.
Heat treatment can affect the magnetic state of the NiFeCoCrPdx system, so matched heat treatment is important for comparison.
The coercivity increase should hold near room temperature when heat treatment and cooling rate are held constant.
The predicted coercivity increase requires avoidance of phase segregation and deleterious secondary phases.
A greater than 10% coercive-field increase relative to the matched baseline is the proposed positive outcome threshold.

contradictions.description: The proposed mechanism emphasizes Pd-induced local magnetic variation and heterogeneity, while the uncertainty field acknowledges that Pd additions reduce exchange-energy variability and increase magnetic homogeneity. These are not necessarily strictly incompatible because structural and exchange heterogeneity differ, but the hypothesis does not reconcile the opposing trends.
